subject: On-prem control plane segregation — risk assessment & runbook alignment
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@edgeworks.com>, EdgeWorks Solutions <eng@edgeworks.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: On-prem control plane segregation — risk assessment & runbook alignment

Samir / EdgeWorks team,

Thanks for the topology you shared last week. We kicked off an internal review focused on the control plane / data plane boundary for the on-prem VPC deployment you requested. Attached is a first-pass diagram (controlplane-segmentation-v1.pdf) and a short checklist of evidence we need for our security review.

High level asks:
- Confirm whether control-plane components (api-server, placement/orch, auth services) will be on a separate VLAN / physical tier from runtime inference nodes, or if they share a common L2/L3 domain.
- If using shared networks, provide the proposed isolation mechanisms (VRF, VLAN tags, tunnel endpoints) and ACL examples.
- Confirm certificate provisioning and rotation approach for control-plane mTLS (who runs the CA, rotation frequency, tooling).
- Egress model: will control plane talk out to the public internet for updates/telemetry, or use a relay in the customer DMZ?

Please respond with the short answers inline and any supporting artifacts by EOD Friday. We want to finalize the runbook alignment and handoff owners so the Private deployment team can prepare the canary.

Also looping Jonas and Karthik for our operational constraints (scaling, observability). Naomie, FYI for compliance evidence gating.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments: controlplane-segmentation-v1.pdf (diagram, 2 pages)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Samir Patel <samir@edgeworks.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: On-prem control plane segregation — risk assessment & runbook alignment

Marissa / Samir — quick clarifications from the runtime side:

1) If control plane and runtimes must share a physical rack (customer constraint), we need explicit L3 segmentation and host-level firewalling. A simple VLAN alone is not sufficient for our KV cache and telemetry tunnels because of broadcast/ARP exposure during failover.

2) We prefer control-plane management APIs to be reachable only via an internal bastion/relay in the management VLAN. Any direct control-plane egress should be restricted to a small set of destinations (Redwood controllers for metrics and model updates).

3) Cert rotation: we can support either (a) customer-run PKI with API to Redwood for cert signing, or (b) Redwood-managed short-lived certs via ACME-style issuance. If EdgeWorks prefers customer PKI for compliance, we need an automated signing endpoint (SCEP/EST) exposed to our control-plane bootstrap.

Can Samir confirm which of these options EdgeWorks will choose? If customer PKI, share endpoint and sample CSR workflow. If Redwood-managed, confirm outbound-relay with IPS allowlist so our issuance calls succeed.

-Jonas
Principal Architect, Inference Runtime

On Tue, Sep 12, 2028 at 09:12 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> (see above)

From: Samir Patel <samir@edgeworks.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: EdgeWorks Solutions <eng@edgeworks.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 14:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem control plane segregation — risk assessment & runbook alignment

Marissa / Jonas — thanks for the notes. Quick answers inline below.

1) Segmentation approach: control-plane services will be deployed into a dedicated management VLAN (VLAN 410). Runtimes will be on VLAN 120/130. Both VLANs traverse the same TOR but are separated with VRF-lite and ACLs on the aggregation switch. We will add host-based firewalls for the control-plane hosts as a secondary enforce.

2) Bastion/relay: yes — we'll put a management relay in the DMZ for outbound control-plane flows. That relay will NAT to a static egress IP and sit behind the customer's perimeter.

3) PKI/cert rotation: customer-run PKI. We expose an EST endpoint for automated signing. Attached is a sample CSR flow and our internal key-rotation cadence (edgeworks-topology-notes.zip). ETA for sharing the EST endpoint details: Weds 9/13 EOD.

4) Egress: control-plane telemetry will go through the relay; we'll provide firewall rules to allow Redwood's telemetry/updates (list of IPs in the related HubSpot ticket).

Next steps:
- We'll upload EST endpoint info + ACL examples to your Drive link by Wed EOD.
- Marissa / Jonas, confirm whether the relay + EST meet your compliance checklist; if yes we'll document in the runbook and schedule a handoff call.

Cheers,
Samir Patel
Eng Manager, Platform Integrations
EdgeWorks Solutions

Attachments: edgeworks-topology-notes.zip (CSR examples, ACL snippets)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir@edgeworks.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Sep 2028 16:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem control plane segregation — risk assessment & runbook alignment

Samir — appreciate the quick turnaround and the attachments. Summary and agreed actions: 

- Segmentation model accepted: VLAN (410) + VRF-lite + switch ACLs + host firewall for defense-in-depth.
- Relay/NAT pattern accepted for egress; EdgeWorks to provide static egress IP(s) and firewall rule text.
- Customer-run PKI via EST is acceptable. EdgeWorks to share EST endpoint, test CSR flow, and a sample signed cert by 2028-09-15.

Owners and next milestones:
- EdgeWorks (Samir): EST endpoint, ACL snippets, static egress IP list — due 2028-09-13 EOD (owner: Samir Patel).
- Redwood (Jonas): Validate CSR flow against our bootstrap process; provide any small code shims if the EST endpoint has nonstandard auth — due 2028-09-14 EOD (owner: Jonas Weber).
- Redwood (Karthik): Draft runbook section (control-plane segregation + cert rotation) and link acceptance criteria to compliance evidence — due 2028-09-16 EOD (owner: Karthik Iyer).
- Compliance (Naomi): Gap check against SOC 2 evidence items and report blocking items — due 2028-09-17 EOD (owner: Naomi Feldman).

If everyone agrees, I'll schedule a 45-min handoff call for Thu 9/14 at 10:00 PT and attach the runbook draft to the Drive link: https://drive.google.com/open?id=1a2b3cControlPlaneSeg.

Thanks — we'll treat this as high priority for the Private pilot.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Manager, Deployments
Redwood Inference

Attachments referenced: controlplane-segmentation-v1.pdf, edgeworks-topology-notes.zip
